chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from his father who said:

I bought camels while I was residing in Al-Medina, and they fascinated me with an intense fascination. So I went to Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) and mentioned them to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it to you and the camels? Did you not know that they are full of misfortunes?'
He said: So from my fascination with them, I hired them out and sent them with some of my servants to Al-Kufa. He said: Then they all perished. So I went to him and informed him.
So he said: 'Therefore let those who go against his command beware lest a trial afflict them or there befalls them a painful punishment.' [Quran 24:63]

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ: Abu al-Hasan the First — a title for Imam Musa al-Kazim (as), the seventh Imam
key_terms.الْمَصَائِبِ: misfortunes/calamities — referring to the many troubles associated with camel ownership
key_terms.عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: painful punishment — Quranic phrase indicating divine retribution
key_terms.فِتْنَةٌ: trial/affliction — a Quranic term for severe tribulation

ai.seo_question: What happened when a companion of Imam al-Kazim bought camels against the Imam's advice?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts how a companion of Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon him) bought camels in Medina, became excessively attached to them, and was warned by the Imam about their misfortunes. Despite the warning, he proceeded to hire them out and send them to Kufa, whereupon all of them perished. When he reported back to the Imam, the Imam quoted Quran 24:63 as a reminder that disobeying the Imam's guidance brings trial and punishment. The hadith teaches that the Imam's words carry the weight of divine guidance, and attachment to worldly acquisitions against the Imam's advice leads to loss.
